threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, objectives, and initial roles for the internship programme.

messages.text:
Kicking off the Inclusive Hospitality Internship Programme Design channel for project_pack_ref: Inclusive Hospitality Internship Programme Design.

Our draft objective is: design and pilot an inclusive internship programme in hospitality services for students from diverse backgrounds, aligned with education policy and evidence-based social research, within 21 days.

I would like us to confirm both the objective and what success for the pilot looks like, and also start narrowing down which hotels or types of hotels we should approach first.

From my side I will be leading T2 and T7, but I will need close input from sociologists, the lecturer, the porter and the journalist.

Can you all react here with your first thoughts on the objective and any constraints we should keep in mind before I move ahead with the framework outline and partner mapping?

Thanks for opening this. From a research side, I will focus on T1 and later T4 and T10.

For the objective, I suggest we make success for the pilot very concrete: for example, a small number of students completing a structured internship cycle in hotels, with basic monitoring data collected and no major operational incidents.

I will start a rapid needs assessment for A1, talking to at least a few students, hotel staff and education staff. Before I do, are there any specific policy or operational questions you want me to probe so that A1 directly feeds into your work on T2 and T7?

From the hotel floor perspective, the objective sounds good as long as we keep disruption low during peak hours.

For the pilot, I would call it a success if interns can safely handle a defined set of front-of-house and back-of-house tasks with clear supervision, and if hotel staff feel the handbook and checklists are easy to use.

On hotel types for T7, I would recommend starting with mid-size city hotels that already host trainees or volunteers. They usually have some structure but are still flexible. I can help you, 52968, by listing a few realistic task bundles per hotel type once we get first findings from A1.

From the academic side, I will work on T5 and T9.

For the objective, could we also include that the internship should contribute to students meeting at least some programme learning outcomes, not just work experience? That will help when we later map activities to credits.

I am not fully sure yet how many hours we can realistically fit into one term without clashing with classes, so I would prefer if we keep the pilot duration modest at first. Maybe we can refine that once we see your draft framework for T2.

I will take the lead on T6 and T8.

On the objective, I would add that success also means the story is understood correctly by students, hotels and the public. We should avoid any impression that interns are cheap labour or that only certain groups are being singled out.

Once we agree on the objective and pilot scope, I will start drafting key messages for A6 and later short summaries for non-specialists. It would help if you, 36727, can share early insights from A1 so we can reflect real concerns in the communication.

I can support on the research design side with 36727 and also review materials for clarity.

For the pilot objective, I would phrase success around three points: inclusive access for diverse students, regulatory compliance, and usable evidence for future scaling.

Maybe we can agree that the pilot should involve a small but mixed group of students, at least two hotels, and a basic pre and post data collection, which will later feed into A5 and A8.

This is helpful. For A1, could you please probe three areas:

1) Barriers students from different backgrounds face when considering hospitality internships.
2) What hotel staff see as realistic intern tasks that do not slow down operations, especially during peak hours.
3) Any concerns about contracts, insurance or working time that might affect compliance.

If we capture those, it will make it easier for me to shape T2 and T7 in line with regulations and hotel realities.

Got it. I will structure the rapid needs assessment for T1 around those three areas.

Plan is: short online survey for students, plus 3 to 4 quick interviews with hotel and education staff. I will keep the questions simple so we can move fast and still have enough depth for A1.

I will share a short outline of the questions in this channel before fielding them, in case anyone wants to add or adjust items.

On hotel types for the pilot under T7, I agree with starting with mid-size city hotels. I would also add one smaller independent hotel if possible. They often have more flexibility to test new approaches and can give us rich feedback for A1 and later A3.

For success criteria, I suggest we track at least: intern attendance and completion, feedback from interns and supervisors, and any incidents or near misses related to safety or guest experience.

I like the idea of a small but mixed group of students and at least two hotels.

One question: do we already have a sense of how many hours per week hotels can realistically host interns without affecting peak operations? That will influence how we frame the academic side in T9.

Maybe we can tentatively say something like 10 to 15 hours per week and then adjust once we hear back from hotel contacts in T7.

From my experience, 10 to 12 hours per week is manageable if we schedule interns outside the busiest breakfast and check-in windows. For example, late morning and mid-afternoon shifts work well for learning without too much pressure.

We should avoid assigning interns to solo night shifts or high-risk tasks. I can detail this more when we work on T3 and T11, but for now this range seems realistic for the pilot.

On success criteria from a communication angle, I propose we also track whether students and hotel staff can accurately describe the programme goals after the initial briefing.

We can include a couple of simple questions in the pre and post tools that 36727 and 45096 will design for A5, to see if our messages land as intended.

This will help us refine A6 and later the summaries under T8.

Yes, we can integrate a few short items on understanding of programme goals into the survey tools for A5.

That will also support the evaluation of inclusion aspects, for example whether students feel the programme is welcoming and fair.

We just need to keep the tools short so hotel staff and students are willing to complete them during a busy term.

Let me try to summarise what I am hearing so far and see if we can close on the pilot objective.

Proposed objective for the pilot: design and run a small-scale, inclusive hospitality internship in 2 to 3 hotels, where a mixed group of students complete a structured cycle of around 10 to 12 hours per week, with clear safeguards, no major operational incidents, and basic pre and post data collection to inform future scaling.

If you agree, I will treat this as our working objective and success criteria for D1 and reflect it in the draft framework for T2.

This wording works for me. It gives us a clear target for A1 and later A5 without locking us into a rigid model.

I will use this objective when framing the needs assessment questions for T1 so that we can test whether stakeholders see it as realistic and inclusive.

I am comfortable with that objective and success description as long as we keep the list of allowed tasks aligned with safety and guest expectations.

From the hotel side, the key is that interns are supervised and not left alone with complex or risky duties. We can refine that in detail under T3 and T11, but the overall direction for D1 looks good.

I agree with the proposed objective and success criteria.

The 10 to 12 hours per week range is manageable from an academic timetable perspective, and we can later translate that into credits or recognition in T9.

So from my side, D1 is fine as you phrased it.

I am also on board with that objective.

It gives us a clear story to tell: a focused pilot in a few hotels, with clear safeguards and learning goals. That will help shape A6 and later the public-facing parts of A8.

No changes from my side for D1.

On hotel selection for the pilot under T7, I hear two main points: focus on mid-size city hotels that already have some experience with trainees, and include at least one smaller independent hotel if possible.

Unless there are objections, I suggest we define D2 as: target 2 to 3 hotels, primarily mid-size city hotels with prior trainee experience, plus one independent hotel if feasible.

I will start mapping potential partners accordingly for T7 and share a shortlist before any formal outreach.

That definition for D2 works for me.

When you have a draft list for T7, I can quickly flag which hotels are more likely to cope with interns without heavy disruption, based on their layout and staffing patterns.

Agreed on D2.

For A1, I will make sure to include at least one staff member from a mid-size hotel and, if possible, someone from a smaller independent hotel, so that our early insights match the types of hotels we are targeting in T7.

threads.thread_goal: Co-create the internship framework and ensure policy and academic alignment.

messages.text:
As a follow-up to our kickoff, I am sharing a first outline for the internship programme framework that will become A2 and feed into T2.

Key elements I am proposing:
- Duration: 8 to 10 weeks, around 10 to 12 hours per week, aligned with what we discussed.
- Roles: clear responsibilities for students, hotel supervisors, university coordinator, and policy contact.
- Safeguards: compliance with education and labour rules, including working time, insurance, and non-discrimination.

Before I draft the full text for A2, I would like feedback on this structure and on how we should map activities to academic requirements for T9. Please share any concerns or additions, especially around safeguards and learning outcomes.

Thanks for sharing the outline.

On the academic side for T9, I think we should explicitly link internship activities to learning outcomes such as communication with guests, teamwork, and understanding of hospitality operations.

I am not entirely sure how detailed we need to be in A2 versus a separate mapping document, so I would appreciate guidance from 45096 on how much detail is typical in such frameworks.

For A2, I would keep the learning outcomes at a moderate level of detail: a short list of core competencies the internship should support.

Then, in T9, we can create a separate mapping document that links specific hotel tasks to programme learning outcomes and credit or recognition options.

This way, the framework stays readable for non-specialists, and we still have enough detail for academic approval.

From the research side, I suggest we integrate a short section in A2 on monitoring and evaluation, pointing to A5.

We can specify that all internships will include a pre and post survey and, where feasible, a short debrief interview. This will help normalise data collection for hotels and students.

I can draft a paragraph for that section once I have the first version of the evaluation questions under T4.

Looking at the structure, I would recommend that A2 clearly distinguishes between tasks interns can do independently and tasks they can only do under supervision.

This will make it easier later to align A3 and the checklists in A7 with the framework.

We should also mention in the safeguards that interns will receive a basic orientation on accessibility and inclusion, so they are prepared to interact respectfully with diverse guests and colleagues.

For A2, could we also include a short section on communication principles that will later be expanded in A6?

For example, commitments to clear language, avoiding stereotypes, and ensuring that all public materials explain the support available to interns.

This will help keep T6 and T8 aligned with the framework from the start.

These are good points. I will adjust the outline of A2 to include:

- A section on task categories (independent vs supervised), to be detailed later in A3 and A7.
- A short monitoring and evaluation section referencing A5.
- A brief communication principles section that links to A6.

Before I lock the structure for D3, are there any concerns about the proposed duration, roles, or safeguards that we have not yet covered?

No additional concerns from me on duration or roles.

For safeguards, I would just ask that we explicitly mention that participation is voluntary and that students can withdraw without academic penalty, as long as they follow a simple procedure.

This will be important when we later explain the programme in the student training outline for A4.

I agree with the structure you described.

On roles, could we clarify in A2 that the university coordinator is responsible for ensuring that internship tasks remain aligned with academic requirements and that any changes are documented? That will make T9 easier to maintain over time.

Otherwise, I am comfortable moving towards confirming the framework structure for D3.

From the hotel side, the proposed duration and roles look workable.

I would just add that the framework should state that hotels can request adjustments to intern schedules during exceptional peak periods, in coordination with the university coordinator.

This will help avoid friction later and can be reflected in both A3 and the daily checklists in A7.

No objections from me.

I will make sure that the evaluation tools in A5 reflect the roles and safeguards described in A2, so that we can later see whether they are working as intended.

Once you have a near-final structure, please share it so I can align T4 accordingly.

Based on your feedback, I propose we confirm the structure of the internship framework for D3 as follows:

- Section 1: Objectives and scope of the pilot.
- Section 2: Duration and schedule (8 to 10 weeks, 10 to 12 hours per week, with flexibility for peak periods).
- Section 3: Roles and responsibilities (students, hotel supervisors, university coordinator, policy contact).
- Section 4: Safeguards and compliance (working time, insurance, non-discrimination, voluntary participation, withdrawal process).
- Section 5: Task categories (independent vs supervised), to be detailed in A3 and A7.
- Section 6: Monitoring and evaluation overview, referencing A5.
- Section 7: Communication principles, referencing A6.

If there are no strong objections, I will proceed with this structure for A2 under T2.

This structure works for me, and it gives us a clear place to connect academic requirements later.

For D3, I support confirming this framework outline.

I also support this structure for D3.

Once you have a draft of A2, I can review the safeguards and roles sections to ensure they are consistent with typical academic and ethical expectations.

From a communication angle, this structure is clear and gives us a solid base for A6.

I agree with confirming it for D3.

No objections from me. The explicit task categories and flexibility for peak periods are especially important for hotels.

So I am fine with confirming D3 as you summarised it.

On mapping internship activities to academic requirements for D4, I propose the following approach for T9:

- We define 4 to 5 core learning outcomes in A2.
- For each outcome, we list typical hotel tasks (from A3 and A7) that contribute to it.
- We then specify how many hours or types of tasks are needed for students to receive credit or a certificate.

Does this sound reasonable, or are we overcomplicating it for a pilot?

I think this is a good and manageable approach for D4.

For the pilot, we can keep the mapping relatively simple: for example, specify that completing the internship with satisfactory feedback on key tasks corresponds to a certain number of hours of practical training or a pass or fail recognition.

We can refine the granularity later if the programme is scaled up.

From an evaluation perspective, a simple mapping is easier to monitor.

If we define a small set of learning outcomes and link them to observable tasks, we can design A5 to capture whether students actually had the chance to perform those tasks and how confident they felt.

So I support your proposal for D4.

This mapping approach is workable from the hotel side as long as we do not create a very complex tracking system for supervisors.

If we can keep it to a short checklist linked to A7, supervisors can quickly confirm which tasks interns have practiced, which will then feed into the academic recognition under T9.

Let me capture D4 based on this discussion.

For the pilot, we will map internship activities to academic requirements by: defining a small set of core learning outcomes in A2, linking them to typical hotel tasks described in A3 and A7, and recognising completion through a simple pass or fail or fixed credit equivalent, based on supervisor checklists and student reflection.

I will reflect this approach in the relevant section of A2 and leave the detailed mapping document to T9.

threads.thread_goal: Define practical hotel operations, intern tasks, and risk mitigation.

messages.text:
I am sharing a first draft list of feasible intern tasks and daily routines from the hotel side, which will feed into A3, A7, T3 and T11.

Proposed task categories:

Front-of-house (mostly supervised at first):
- Greeting guests in the lobby and directing them to reception.
- Assisting with simple check-in or check-out steps under staff guidance.
- Helping prepare welcome materials and information stands.

Back-of-house (some independent, some supervised):
- Preparing and restocking housekeeping trolleys.
- Sorting laundry and amenities.
- Supporting simple breakfast prep tasks that do not involve sharp tools or hot surfaces.

I have also started listing common operational risks (for example, slips and falls, data privacy at reception, guest complaints) and basic mitigation steps for T11.

Please react with what feels realistic, what should be removed, and what we might be missing.

This looks like a solid starting point.

From a research and inclusion angle, I would suggest we also consider tasks that allow interns to interact with diverse guests in a structured way, for example supporting information desks or feedback collection, as long as they are trained.

For T11, could you share more detail on how you see data privacy risks at reception and what simple rules we can include in A3 so interns do not accidentally see or share sensitive information?

Thanks for structuring this so clearly.

From a regulatory perspective, we should avoid assigning interns to tasks that could be interpreted as full responsibility for cash handling, security, or unsupervised night shifts.

In A3, could we mark such tasks as explicitly excluded for interns, so that hotels do not accidentally cross a line when implementing the pilot?

Looking at these tasks from an academic perspective, they align well with learning outcomes around communication, teamwork, and understanding hotel operations.

For T9, it would help if we can group tasks into a few clusters, such as guest interaction, operational support, and back-of-house logistics. That will make it easier to map them to learning outcomes later.

I do not see any major issues, but I am less familiar with the operational risks, so I will rely on you and 36727 to flag anything critical for T11.

I agree this is a good starting list.

For inclusion, we might want to ensure that there are tasks suitable for students with different physical or sensory needs. For example, some roles could focus more on coordination, documentation, or digital tasks rather than physical work.

Could we add a note in A3 that hotels should, where possible, offer at least one lower-physical-intensity task option per intern?

From a communication standpoint, it will be important that the tasks we list in A3 and A7 are easy to explain to students and hotel staff.

Once you have a more detailed draft, I can help simplify the wording for non-specialists under T8, so that the checklists are clear and do not feel intimidating.

On data privacy at reception, the main risks are interns seeing full ID documents, credit card details, or sensitive notes in the system.

In A3, I propose we include simple rules such as: interns do not handle payment cards, do not read or enter sensitive notes, and only observe or assist with non-sensitive parts of check-in, like confirming breakfast times or explaining facilities.

For T11, I will list data privacy as a specific risk with these mitigation steps.

Agreed on excluding cash handling, security, and unsupervised night shifts.

I will create a short list of explicitly excluded tasks in A3 and mirror that in the risk section for T11, so hotels have a clear red line.

This will also help us communicate to students what they should not be asked to do.

I like the idea of explicitly including lower-physical-intensity tasks.

From the needs assessment work for A1, I am already hearing that some students are concerned about physically demanding roles.

If we can show in A3 that there are options like documentation, guest feedback collection, or digital tasks, it may increase participation from diverse groups.

Good point. I will add a cluster of tasks around guest feedback and simple digital admin, such as helping prepare event boards, updating printed information, or supporting basic survey distribution.

These can be done in quieter areas and adapted to different physical abilities.

For the clusters you mentioned, I can later use them in T9 to show how each group of tasks supports specific learning outcomes.

It might be helpful if A7 reflects the same clusters, so supervisors can quickly see which learning areas each shift covers.

Let me propose a more concrete list of allowed tasks for D5, grouped into clusters:

Guest interaction (supervised): greeting guests, giving basic directions, explaining breakfast times and facilities, supporting feedback collection with a simple script.

Operational support (partly independent): preparing and restocking housekeeping trolleys, sorting laundry and amenities, setting up meeting rooms, restocking public area supplies.

Back-of-house logistics (partly independent): simple breakfast prep without direct exposure to hot surfaces or sharp tools, basic stock checks, preparing welcome materials.

Excluded tasks: cash handling, unsupervised night shifts, security duties, handling payment cards, and accessing sensitive guest data.

If this list works for you, we can treat it as the agreed scope of intern tasks for D5 and I will embed it in A3 and A7 under T3.

This list looks balanced and consistent with regulatory expectations.

For D5, I support confirming these clusters and exclusions as the official list of allowed tasks for the pilot.

Please just make sure that in A3 we clearly label the excluded tasks so hotels do not miss them.

I also support this list for D5.

It gives us enough variety for learning while keeping risks manageable. I will reference these clusters when designing the evaluation questions in A5, so we can see which types of tasks interns actually performed.

From the academic side, this list is clear and aligns well with the learning outcomes we discussed.

I am comfortable confirming it for D5 and will use these clusters in T9.

This list is also easy to explain in communication materials.

Once A3 and A7 are drafted, I can help turn these clusters into simple bullet points for students and hotels under T8.

On risk mitigation and onboarding steps for D6, here is what I propose for T11 and A7:

Onboarding steps:
- Short safety tour of the hotel, including emergency exits and restricted areas.
- Briefing on data privacy rules and guest confidentiality.
- Introduction to the supervisor and buddy system.

Risk mitigation measures:
- Interns always have a named supervisor on shift.
- Clear list of excluded tasks posted in the staff area.
- Simple incident reporting form for any safety or guest issues.

If we agree on this package, I will integrate it into A3 and the checklists in A7.

I support this onboarding and risk mitigation package for D6.

It is simple enough for hotels to implement and gives us a clear baseline when we later analyse incidents or feedback in A5.

This set of measures is aligned with typical expectations for internships.

For D6, I agree to confirm these onboarding steps and risk mitigation measures as standard for all pilot hotels.

I also agree with this package for D6.

We can echo the key onboarding points in the training outlines for A4, so students hear them both at the university and at the hotel.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize evaluation tools and data collection approach for the pilot.

messages.text:
I am sharing a draft evaluation plan and survey templates for the pilot, which will become part of A5 under T4 and T10.

Key elements:

Evaluation questions:
- To what extent does the internship improve students confidence and understanding of hotel operations?
- How inclusive and supportive do students and hotel staff perceive the programme to be?
- Are the agreed tasks and safeguards (from A2 and A3) implemented as planned?

Tools:
- Pre-internship survey for students (short online form).
- Post-internship survey for students and hotel supervisors.
- Optional short debrief interview guide.

I have kept the wording simple and limited the number of questions to keep the burden low. I would appreciate feedback on indicators, missing questions, and any ethical or privacy concerns before we finalise for D7.

Thanks for pulling this together.

From an ethics and privacy perspective, I would suggest we:
- Avoid collecting any directly identifying information in the surveys beyond what is strictly needed for analysis.
- Include a short consent statement at the start of each tool, explaining purpose, voluntary participation, and data handling.

I can review the final wording to ensure it aligns with typical academic standards before we sign off on D7.

Looking at the evaluation questions, I think they cover the essentials.

For academic alignment, could we add one or two items that ask students to self-assess their progress on the core learning outcomes we defined in A2 and will map in T9?

This will help us see whether the internship is contributing to those outcomes from the students perspective.

From a policy and programme management angle, I would like to see at least one indicator on hotel willingness to continue or expand the programme.

Maybe a simple question in the supervisor survey asking whether they would host interns again and what changes they would suggest.

This will be useful later when we compile A8 and consider scaling.

From the hotel floor perspective, shorter is better.

If we can keep the supervisor survey to around 5 to 7 quick questions, mostly multiple choice with one open comment box, it will increase the chances that busy staff complete it.

I would also suggest including one question about whether the onboarding and risk mitigation steps from A3 and A7 were actually followed in practice.

I can help simplify the language of the survey questions later under T8.

For now, I would just suggest we include one or two items checking whether students and staff feel they understood the programme goals and support available, so we can test the effectiveness of A6.

We should avoid jargon and keep response options clear and concrete.

Thanks for the ethics pointers.

I will adjust the tools so that we only collect minimal identifiers and add a short consent statement at the start of each survey and interview guide.

Once I have updated drafts, I will share them for your review before we finalise D7.

Good idea on linking to learning outcomes.

I will add a short block in the student surveys where they rate their confidence on 3 to 4 core outcomes from A2, both before and after the internship.

This will give us a simple way to see perceived progress without making the tools too long.

I will add a question in the supervisor survey asking whether they would host interns again and what they would change.

We can later use these responses directly in A8 when summarising recommendations for scaling.

Understood on survey length.

I will keep the supervisor survey to a maximum of 7 questions, mostly multiple choice, and include one item on whether onboarding and risk mitigation steps from A3 and A7 were followed.

We can test the timing during T10 when we pilot the tools with a small group.

Once you have the updated drafts, please send them my way.

I will check that the consent language is clear and that the questions do not inadvertently pressure students or staff to give only positive feedback.

When you are ready, I can also do a quick pass on the wording to remove any technical terms and make sure the questions are easy to understand for non-specialists.

This will also help us keep the tone consistent with A6 and other public-facing materials.

I have now incorporated your suggestions into the evaluation plan and tools in A5:

- Minimal identifiers and clear consent statements.
- Items on learning outcomes, inclusion, understanding of programme goals, and willingness of hotels to continue.
- Supervisor survey limited to 7 questions, mostly multiple choice.

Before we finalise D7, are there any remaining concerns about indicators or question types?

No further concerns from me.

The added items on learning outcomes and inclusion cover what I needed from an academic perspective.

I am comfortable moving to approval for D7.

I have reviewed the updated drafts and the consent language looks clear and appropriate.

The balance between closed and open questions also seems reasonable.

From my side, we can approve the indicators and survey questions for D7.

I am satisfied that the tools will give us the information we need for programme decisions and for A8.

I support approving the current set of indicators and survey questions for D7.

From the hotel side, the tools look manageable and the questions are understandable.

I agree with approving them for D7.

I have no further edits on the content.

Once we start T10, I can help check if any questions still feel confusing to respondents and adjust wording if needed, but for now I also support D7.

threads.thread_goal: Align on communication strategy and public narrative for the programme.

messages.text:
I am sharing draft key messages and a communication plan outline for A6 under T6.

Key messages (for students, hotels, and public):
- The programme offers structured, supported internships in hospitality for students from diverse backgrounds.
- Hotels and universities work together to ensure fair conditions, learning opportunities, and respect for all participants.
- The pilot is small-scale and evidence-based, with clear monitoring through A5 and a summary in A8.

Channels:
- Internal: university mailing lists, student support channels, and direct outreach to partner hotels.
- External: a short web article, social media posts, and possibly a local press note once the pilot is underway.

I would like your feedback on tone, missing points, and which channels we should prioritise before we sign off on D8.

Thanks for drafting this.

From a policy perspective, I would like the messages to emphasise that the programme complies with education and labour regulations and that it is a partnership, not a replacement for regular staff.

For channels, I suggest we prioritise internal university and hotel communications first, and only move to broader media once the pilot is running smoothly.

From the research side, it would be helpful if we mention that the pilot is being monitored through simple surveys and feedback tools, without making it sound heavy or intrusive.

This can reassure stakeholders that we are learning from the pilot and that their input matters, which will later feed into A8.

For students, I would highlight three things clearly:
- What they can expect to learn.
- What support they will receive.
- How the internship links to their studies or recognition.

This will connect the communication plan with the training outlines in A4 and the mapping in T9.

I agree with the points raised so far.

I would also suggest we avoid any language that could be interpreted as targeting only one specific group of students. Instead, we can say that the programme is designed to be inclusive and supportive of diverse backgrounds.

This will help avoid misinterpretation in external channels.

From the hotel side, it would be useful if the messages to hotels clearly state:
- The expected time commitment.
- The support they will receive (handbook A3, checklists A7, contact points).
- The benefits, such as fresh perspectives and potential future staff.

This can help address concerns about operational burden.

Thanks for the input.

I will adjust the key messages to explicitly mention regulatory compliance and clarify that interns complement, not replace, staff.

For channels, I agree we start with internal communications and only consider a press note once we have some early positive feedback from the pilot.

I will add a short line in the messages explaining that we use simple surveys and feedback tools to learn from the pilot, without going into technical detail.

This will connect the communication plan with A5 and A8 without overwhelming readers.

For students, I will structure the message around learn, support, and recognition, and cross-check with the training outlines in A4 and the mapping in T9 once they are drafted.

This should help keep a consistent story across documents.

For hotels, I will highlight the time commitment, support materials (A3 and A7), and potential benefits, as you suggested.

I will keep the language practical and avoid any marketing tone that might feel unrealistic to hotel managers.

On channels for D8, I propose we formally agree on the following for the pilot:

Primary channels:
- Internal university and student support channels.
- Direct communication with partner hotels.

Secondary channels (after initial feedback):
- University website article.
- Limited social media posts.

We can keep the option of a local press note open but only use it if the pilot runs smoothly and leadership is comfortable.

This channel mix makes sense to me.

It gives us enough visibility to recruit students and hotels while keeping expectations manageable during the pilot.

I support using these channels for D8.

I agree with prioritising internal channels and a university website article.

This will also make it easier to direct students to more detailed information and training materials in A4.

From the hotel side, direct communication is key.

I support the proposed channels for D8, especially direct emails or calls to hotel managers with a clear, concise information sheet.

I am also comfortable with this channel strategy for D8.

It balances transparency with caution while we are still in a pilot phase.

Based on the feedback, I will finalise A6 with:

- Key messages that emphasise inclusion, learning, regulatory compliance, and partnership.
- Tailored sections for students, hotels, and the public.
- The agreed channel strategy for D8, starting with internal and direct communications, then a website article and limited social media.

Once the pilot is complete, I will also support 52968 in reflecting these messages in A8 under T12.
